runtime_notes: README documents interactive deployment through `adk web --port 4200`.
Document AI execution requires GCP project/location/processor credentials and an enabled processor.

authority_facts.fact: The ADK agent binds `process_document_with_ocr` and `search_document` directly as model-callable tools.

`process_document_with_ocr(document_path)` accepts an absolute path unchanged, or joins any relative path to the project root, then opens the resulting path with `open(..., 'rb')` without a containment/allowlist check.

The bytes read from the selected file are placed into a Google Document AI RawDocument and sent to `process_document`; therefore a model-selected readable local path can cause file content to cross an external service boundary.
The agent prompt says documents are in `data/sample/` and asks the assistant to confirm paths, but that restriction is not enforced in tool code.

findings.claim: Interactive agent input can induce a model tool call with a path outside the intended sample directory; the tool reads that local file and submits its bytes to Google Document AI. Source contains no path-containment or file allowlist enforcement.
evidence: agent.py: root_agent tools include process_document_with_ocr and search_document
tools/document_ocr.py: absolute paths are accepted unchanged and relative paths are joined to project root
tools/document_ocr.py: open(document_path, 'rb') reads the selected file
tools/document_ocr.py: RawDocument(content=document_content) is sent through process_document
README.md: interactive deployment documented via adk web

chain: local file read outside intended sample directory

controls: Prompt text recommends `data/sample/` paths and asks the model to confirm the document path.
The file must exist and Document AI credentials/runtime dependencies must be configured.

runtime_notes: Both configured MCP servers are active in the checked-in config but require EXA_API_KEY/FIRECRAWL_API_KEY.
The committed `__main__` entrypoint uses a fixed research prompt rather than reading CLI/web user input.

authority_facts.fact: The LangGraph ReAct agent is created with `client.get_tools()` from every successfully connected active MCP server.
The Firecrawl MCP exposes scrape_url, crawl_website, map_website and extract_structured_data with model-supplied URL/URL-list parameters and no source-visible destination allowlist.
The Exa tools are provider-mediated search; query/domain filters do not give the model a direct arbitrary socket destination.
At the pinned entrypoint there is no source-proven untrusted runtime ingress because the query passed to main() is a constant.

findings.claim: When the configured Firecrawl MCP is available, the model has source-proven authority to select arbitrary URL targets for scrape/crawl/map/extract operations without a destination allowlist. The pinned entrypoint does not expose this authority to untrusted user input.
evidence: servers/fire_crawl.py: scrape_url(url), crawl_website(url), map_website(url), extract_structured_data(urls, ...) accept caller-selected destinations
servers/fire_crawl.py: no URL allowlist/private-network restriction is visible
findings.reachability: effective_if_firecrawl_credentials_present; no untrusted ingress proven at pinned entrypoint

controls: Firecrawl performs the remote fetch through a provider SDK rather than a direct requests/httpx call from the local application.
The committed main entrypoint supplies a fixed query, so this batch does not assert an attacker-controlled end-to-end path.

runtime_notes: The CLI requires REDMINE_URL and REDMINE_API_KEY, plus a reachable local Ollama-compatible endpoint.
The REPL provides source-proven user input to the custom model/tool loop.

authority_facts.fact: CLI input enters Agent.chat(), the local LLM receives a fixed catalogue of five Redmine tools, and model tool calls are name-validated before MCP dispatch.
Every exposed Redmine tool is read-only: projects/issues/time entries ultimately use HTTP GET against paths under a configured Redmine base URL.
No issue update/create/delete, time-entry mutation, filesystem write, process-execution or arbitrary destination tool is exposed in the reviewed effective catalogue.

controls: Tool names are checked against TOOL_NAMES before dispatch.
MCP server exposes only read operations.
Redmine requests use a configured authenticated base URL rather than model-selected hosts.
This is a precision-control case: untrusted CLI ingress plus authenticated data.read authority should not become state-change/process/broad-destination findings.

runtime_notes: The committed main entrypoint uses fixed SCAN_DIR/REPORT_PATH values and a fixed instruction prompt.
Repository source files are intentionally read and returned into the model context.

authority_facts.fact: The model is directly bound to list_files, read_file and write_report.
list_files passes a model-selected directory directly to Path(directory).resolve().rglob without enforcing SCAN_DIR containment.
read_file joins SCAN_DIR with a model-selected file_path but never resolves-and-checks the resulting path, so `../` path traversal can escape the intended scan directory.
write_report accepts a model-selected output_path, creates parent directories and writes text without restricting the path to REPORT_PATH or a safe directory.
Contents of scanned source files are returned to the model, creating an indirect untrusted-content channel into a model that holds the above filesystem authority.

findings.claim: The code-review agent feeds repository file content into a model that can select directories/file paths and report output paths without containment enforcement. Malicious or adversarial source content can therefore influence a tool-using model with broader filesystem read/write authority than the intended sample-project/report scope.
evidence: shared_tools.py: list_files_in_directory resolves arbitrary model-selected directory
shared_tools.py: read_file_contents builds base_directory / file_path without containment validation
shared_tools.py: write_todo_report writes Path(output_path) and creates parents
openai-agents/agent.py: source file contents are returned by read_file into the model/tool loop
findings.reachability: source_proven_model_authority; exploitability depends on model response to adversarial repository content

chain: filesystem read outside SCAN_DIR or write outside intended REPORT_PATH

controls: The normal main prompt supplies fixed SCAN_DIR and REPORT_PATH.
The sample repository content reviewed here is ordinary TODO-bearing source, not a demonstrated malicious prompt payload.
No path containment check enforces the intended fixed scope if the model selects a different path.

runtime_notes: The Streamlit app requires Supabase authentication and Groq/Tavily configuration for the relevant flows.
Authenticated chat input is source-proven to reach agent.run_sync.

authority_facts.fact: Authenticated Streamlit user input is passed to the PydanticAI agent through agent.run_sync.
The agent exposes fetch_curriculum(url), whose documented intended use is explicitly a URL supplied by the user.
fetch_curriculum calls httpx.AsyncClient(follow_redirects=True).get(url) with no source-visible host, scheme, private-address or redirect-destination allowlist.
research_domain is provider-mediated Tavily search and is distinct from the direct arbitrary URL fetch authority of fetch_curriculum.

findings.claim: An authenticated user can supply a curriculum URL that the agent may pass to a server-side httpx client with redirects enabled and no destination restriction. This is source-proven broad server-side URL-fetch authority and can include destinations outside the intended public curriculum sites.
evidence: src/agent.py: no host/private-IP/redirect allowlist is enforced

controls: Authentication is required before the main chat page.
System/tool instructions tell the model to call fetch_curriculum only for a URL explicitly supplied by the user; this limits autonomous invention but does not restrict the destination itself.
